abstract:
Angiopoietin-like proteins (ANGPTL) 3 and 4 modulate lipoprotein metabolism through inhibition of lipases. Reduced activity of ANGPTL3 and ANGPTL4 improves kidney function in mice. This study investigated the causal relationships of ANGPTLs and their lipase targets with chronic kidney disease (CKD) in humans.
A drug-target Mendelian randomization (MR) study and single-cell RNA sequencing analyses.
Participants of European, East Asian, and African ancestry in the All of Us, Penn Medicine Biobank, and genome-wide association studies; kidney samples from the Susztaklab Kidney Biobank.
Genetically proxied ANGPTL3, ANGPTL4, lipoprotein lipase, endothelial lipase, and hepatic lipase.
CKD risk and estimated glomerular filtration rate based on serum creatinine (eGFRcr).
Genetic variants were used as proxies for ANGPTLs and their lipase targets, and their associations with CKD risk and eGFRcr were assessed. Relevant gene expression across kidney cell types and between CKD patients and controls was also characterized.
In total, 186,388 CKD cases among 2,369,738 individuals were included. For each 1 SD decrease in triglycerides, genetically proxied ANGPTL3 inhibition, ANGPTL4 inhibition, and lipoprotein lipase enhancement were associated with lower CKD risk (odds ratio [OR], 0.76 [95% CI, 0.69-0.84], 0.78 [95% CI, 0.68-0.91], and 0.86 [95% CI, 0.83-0.90]) and higher eGFRcr. For each 1 SD decrease in high-density lipoprotein cholesterol, genetically proxied endothelial lipase enhancement was associated with lower CKD risk (OR, 0.89 [95% CI, 0.82-0.96]) and higher eGFRcr specifically in people of European ancestry. Genetically proxied hepatic lipase enhancement was associated with lower CKD risk (OR, 0.83 [95% CI, 0.74-0.92]) specifically in people of African ancestry. ANGPTL3, ANGPTL4, and LPL were differentially expressed across kidney cell types and between CKD patients and controls.
Rigorous MR assumptions, non-kidney-specific instrument selection, and potential misclassification of CKD.
Genetic reductions in ANGPTL3 and ANGPTL4 reduce CKD risk by enhancing lipase activity. ANGPTL3, ANGPTL4, and their target lipases (lipoprotein lipase and endothelial lipase) are potentially promising therapeutic targets for CKD prevention and treatment.
Angiopoietin-like proteins (ANGPTL) 3 and 4 modulate blood lipid levels by inhibiting lipase activity. This study investigated whether ANGPTL3 and 4 and their lipase targets affect chronic kidney disease (CKD). It used genetic variants as proxies for ANGPTL3 and 4 and for their target lipases and assessed their associations with CKD risk and kidney function in over 2.3 million individuals. It found that genetic proxies for inhibition of ANGPTL3 and 4, as well as for enhanced activity of lipoprotein lipase and endothelial lipase, were associated with lower risk of CKD and better kidney function. This study suggests that these proteins and lipases are potentially promising therapeutic targets for CKD prevention and treatment.

title: The Role of Angiopoietin-Like Proteins 3 and 4 and Their Target Lipases in CKD: A Drug-Target Mendelian Randomization Study.
